sql-server-reporting-services.title: What Is SQL Server Reporting Services? – Microsoft Learn
sql-server-reporting-services.notes: SQL Server Reporting Services is a set of on-premises tools and services for creating, deploying and managing reports. It covers two report types: paginated reports, which have a fixed layout suited to printing and can be exported to formats such as PDF or Word, and mobile reports, which adapt to different devices and orientations. Paginated reports are authored with Report Builder or with Report Designer in SQL Server Data Tools, while mobile reports are built with the Mobile Report Publisher app and rely on Datazen technology. A web portal, which replaced Report Manager, lets users browse a folder hierarchy, mark favorites, and manage reports, KPIs, Excel workbooks, shared datasets and shared data sources, along with scheduled processing and subscriptions. Recipients can view reports in a browser, on a mobile device or by email. The platform also exposes APIs so developers can integrate and extend report processing in their own applications. The page covers SQL Server 2016 and later, and notes that with SQL Server 2025 the on-premises product is consolidated under Power BI Report Server.

static-code-analysis.title: Legacy analysis for managed code – Visual Studio – Microsoft Learn
static-code-analysis.notes: Microsoft's documentation on legacy static code analysis for managed code describes a tool, also known as FxCop analysis, that inspects compiled managed assemblies without running the program. It reports violations of programming and design rules drawn from the .NET design guidelines and, where possible, suggests how to fix them. Findings show up as warnings. Developers can run the analysis automatically on every build through the project's Code Analysis property page, or start it manually from the Analyze menu. Rule sets decide which checks apply; Microsoft's defaults can be used or custom sets created. Individual warnings can be suppressed in source with the SuppressMessage attribute, and a menu command suppresses all active issues at once, which helps after a migration that floods a project with warnings. Teams can pair it with check-in policies and run it in team builds. A key limit is that this legacy analysis does not support .NET Core or .NET Standard projects, for which the page points to analyzers built on the .NET Compiler Platform.

surrogate-key.title: Modeling Dimension Tables in Warehouse – Microsoft Fabric – Microsoft Learn
surrogate-key.notes: In a dimensional model, a surrogate key is a single-column unique identifier that is generated and stored in a dimension table. It acts as the table's primary key, and fact tables and other tables reference the dimension through it. The documentation lists several reasons to use one: it lets data from multiple sources be consolidated without clashing identifiers, replaces a multi-column natural key with a more efficient single column, keeps fact tables narrow when the smallest suitable integer type is used, and shields the warehouse from changes in source data. It is required for slowly changing dimension type 2, because several versions of the same member would otherwise repeat the natural key. The guidance recommends a surrogate key even when a natural key looks like a good candidate, and says key values should carry no meaning, with date and time dimensions as exceptions. The natural key stays in the table so the dimension can be tied back to the source system. During fact loading, the ETL process looks up keys and returns only current versions, and reserved values mark missing, unknown, not applicable or erroneous members.

teams-developer-portal.title: Teams Developer Portal Overview – Microsoft Learn
teams-developer-portal.notes: Developer Portal for Teams, formerly called App Studio, is the main tool for configuring, distributing and managing Microsoft Teams apps, and it also supports collaborating with colleagues on an app project. Developers can create a new app by giving it a name, or import an existing one from its manifest file; an app already published in the Teams admin center and registered in the portal can be replaced during import. Apps built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit in Visual Studio Code can be managed there, as can apps coming from App Studio. Ownership can be handled by adding owners, and Teams or Global Administrators can claim apps that have no owner. The portal also links to app usage analytics and app validation. Signing in is required. Limits include no availability for GCC High, Department of Defense and 21Vianet-operated tenants, with a workaround of creating the app in a regular tenant and uploading it through Microsoft Graph, and an import error when the package contains nested folders or lacks files. Apps that are published but not registered cannot be imported until an admin files a support ticket.

teams-meeting-apps.title: Designing your meeting extension – Microsoft Learn
teams-meeting-apps.notes: Microsoft's design guidance for Teams meeting extensions explains how apps can make meetings more productive, for instance through polls or brief reminders that do not interrupt the flow. Apps can be added before a meeting through the add-a-tab option in the meeting details, or during a meeting from the More menu on desktop. The surfaces include a meeting tab used before and after the meeting, an in-meeting tab shown as a side panel next to the meeting stage, an in-meeting dialog displayed on the stage and triggered by a user such as the organizer, and a shared meeting stage where app content is shown to all participants in the space used for screen sharing. The share button can be renamed, for example to Play together or Watch together. Dialogs suit short interactions such as quick feedback, approvals or mini polls, while tabs suit evaluations, tasks and notes. Design rules call for single-column layouts, vertical scrolling only, avoiding modals in the side panel, and a look tuned to dark mode. Complex flows belong in the tab rather than a dialog, and another app's dialog cannot appear while your app is on the stage.

threat-actor.title: How Microsoft names threat actors – Microsoft Learn
threat-actor.notes: Microsoft's page on how it names threat actors does not define the term in general, but it describes the kinds of actors it tracks and the naming scheme it uses. It sorts actors into five categories: nation-state actors working for or directed by a government program, financially motivated actors behind activity such as ransomware, business email compromise and phishing, private sector offensive actors that are commercial companies building and selling cyber weapons, influence operations that run manipulative information campaigns, and groups in development, a provisional label for unknown or emerging activity. Names follow a weather-based taxonomy in which the family name signals the category, for example Typhoon for China-linked nation-state activity, Blizzard for Russia, Sandstorm for Iran, Sleet for North Korea and Tempest for financially motivated actors. An adjective distinguishes actors within a family, and the Storm label with a number is used for clusters that are still unclear. The goal is to help organizations prioritize risk and help researchers track threats. Origin attribution is an assessment, and the mapping to other vendors' names is updated over time.

time-to-first-token.title: Azure OpenAI in Microsoft Foundry Models performance & latency – Microsoft Learn
time-to-first-token.notes: The Azure OpenAI performance and latency page treats time to first token as the interval between submitting a prompt and receiving the first token, expressed in milliseconds. It places the metric in a relationship where total response time equals time to first token plus the average gap between tokens multiplied by the number of tokens generated. Larger prompts raise the first-token delay, though the page says prompt size usually matters less than how much text is generated, and heavy deployment load or many simultaneous requests can also slow responses. In Azure Monitor, the Time to Response metric corresponds to time to first token and suits streaming workloads, whereas a normalized variant divides first-byte latency by prompt token count and is meant for comparing across prompt sizes, not for diagnosing absolute latency. Latency metrics should be read together with a token metric such as processed prompt tokens. Streaming shortens the wait for the first output and improves perceived responsiveness in chat interfaces, but it does not change how long the full answer takes, and it matters less for batch jobs. The page gives no concrete target values.

transact-sql.title: Transact-SQL reference (Database Engine) – Microsoft Learn
transact-sql.notes: The Transact-SQL reference for the Database Engine is an entry page to the documentation of Microsoft's SQL dialect, T-SQL. It states that all tools and applications that talk to a SQL Server database do so by sending T-SQL commands, which makes the language central to Microsoft SQL products and services. The reference applies to SQL Server, Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, Azure Synapse Analytics and several Microsoft Fabric items such as the warehouse and the SQL analytics endpoint, although individual articles may be valid only for certain products, as shown in their applies-to notes. Common statements named include SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE. The reference also links system objects such as catalog views, dynamic management views, system functions and system stored procedures, and related languages like XQuery and MDX. Tools that use T-SQL include SQL Server Management Studio, the MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code, SQL Server Data Tools and sqlcmd. In Management Studio, pressing F1 on a keyword opens its reference article. Details on SQL standards support are in a separate document.

trusted-platform-module.title: Trusted Platform Module (TPM) overview – Microsoft Learn
trusted-platform-module.notes: The Trusted Platform Module is a hardware-based security feature: a chip acting as a secure cryptographic processor with several physical tamper-resistance mechanisms, so malware cannot interfere with its protections. Its specifications are defined by the Trusted Computing Group. It generates, stores and limits the use of cryptographic keys, can authenticate a device through a unique RSA key held in the chip, and records measurements of boot components such as firmware and the operating system so a key is usable only when the system started with the expected software. Keys can be set so they never leave the module, and authorization values trigger dictionary-attack protection after too many failed attempts. Windows Hello, BitLocker and System Guard rely on it. Typical uses include certificates bound to the device, replacing smart cards, BitLocker Network Unlock and device health attestation, where an MDM server asks a health service about settings such as Secure Boot. New and upgraded Windows 11 devices need TPM 2.0, and device health attestation with TPM 2.0 requires UEFI firmware. Windows initializes and takes ownership of the TPM automatically.

unconstrained-delegation.title: Account security posture assessments – Microsoft Defender for Identity
unconstrained-delegation.notes: Microsoft Defender for Identity's account posture assessment page covers unsecure Kerberos delegation. Kerberos delegation is a setting that lets an application request end-user credentials in order to reach resources on behalf of the originating user. The page lists three kinds: unconstrained delegation, constrained delegation and resource-based constrained delegation. It does not explain the ticket mechanics of the unconstrained type, but it describes the risk: an entity with unsecure delegation can impersonate a user toward any other service, and any service can be abused if one of its delegation entries is sensitive. As an example, a web site running under an application pool account with unconstrained delegation could, after a domain admin signs in, request a service ticket for a SQL server in that admin's name, and could even change the Enterprise Admins group or obtain the KRBTGT hash. The core problem is having to trust the application to behave correctly, which attackers can exploit. The recommendation is to disable delegation or move to a constrained type, by trusting the computer for delegation to specified services only and listing the services allowed. The assessment concerns entities that are not domain controllers.

unity-catalog.title: What is Unity Catalog? – Azure Databricks – Microsoft Learn
unity-catalog.notes: Unity Catalog is the unified governance layer for data and AI in Azure Databricks. Once enabled for a workspace, it works underneath all data and AI interactions there. It controls access when a table is queried or a model is called, tracks lineage automatically, and records activity for auditing, with access available through Catalog Explorer, SQL, the Databricks CLI and REST APIs. All governed objects are securable objects to which privileges are granted to users, service principals or groups. Tables, views, volumes, functions and models use a three-level namespace of catalog, schema and object. Tables and volumes are either managed, where Unity Catalog handles storage lifecycle and governance, or external, where it handles governance only. Functional areas include access control with attribute-based policies and row and column filters, discovery, lineage, audit logs as a system table, data classification, data quality monitoring, data sharing across organizations and clouds, and AI governance. It is on automatically for workspaces created after November 2023; older workspaces must be upgraded. An open-source implementation also exists, and the page refers to a separate page for requirements and limitations.

vector-store.title: Vector search in Azure AI Search – Microsoft Learn
vector-store.notes: The Azure AI Search page on vector search describes an approach in which content is indexed and queried as numeric vectors, so matches come from similarity to a query vector rather than shared keywords. This makes matches possible by meaning, such as dog and canine, across languages, and across content types like text and images. Text is turned into vectors by embedding models, and queries are encoded the same way. Each vector field gets an internal vector index built on a nearest-neighbors approach, and queries return the closest k neighbors. Embeddings can be created through integrated vectorization in an indexer pipeline, using an indexer, a supported data source and a skillset, or generated externally and written into vector fields. Scenarios include similarity search, hybrid search that combines vector and keyword queries in one request, multimodal and multilingual search, and filtered vector search. The service can also act as a pure vector store serving as long-term memory, a knowledge base or the retrieval layer for retrieval-augmented generation. Vector fields themselves are not filterable, so filtering uses a separate text or numeric field. Services created before 2019 do not support vector workloads.

webauthn.title: WebAuthn APIs for passwordless authentication on Windows – Microsoft Learn
webauthn.notes: The WebAuthn APIs page describes Win32 platform APIs for passwordless authentication on Windows, based on W3C and FIDO2 standards and introduced in Windows 10 version 1903. They let developers use Windows Hello or FIDO2 security keys for passwordless multi-factor sign-in in apps and websites, without handling the USB, NFC and Bluetooth transports themselves, and users can rely on any WebAuthn-capable browser. Roles include the client device, the relying party that consumes strong credentials, the WebAuthn API, the CTAP2 platform that mediates between client and authenticators, platform authenticators built into a device such as fingerprint or face recognition, and roaming authenticators like USB keys or NFC cards. Newer Windows 11 releases add passkey manager APIs that let native apps provide passkeys across browsers and apps. Web applications must go through the browser, while native applications can call the API directly. Limits: Microsoft Account requires FIDO2 CTAP2 capabilities and does not accept CTAP1/U2F credentials, Edge does not speak U2F, Edge on Android does not support WebAuthn, and Microsoft offers no roaming authenticator of its own.

windows-server-update-services.title: Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) overview – Microsoft Learn
windows-server-update-services.notes: Windows Server Update Services is a server role that lets IT administrators deploy Microsoft product updates, managing the distribution of updates published through Microsoft Update to computers on the network. The stated aims of update management are operational efficiency, protection against vulnerabilities and a stable production environment. Administration happens through a management console, and PowerShell cmdlets cover the main tasks and allow routine administration to be automated. SHA-256 is supported for added security, the Windows Update Agent can be deployed independently of the server, and one WSUS server can serve as the update source for other WSUS servers. At least one WSUS server in the network must be able to connect to Microsoft Update to learn which updates exist; how many servers connect directly is left to the administrator. The page lists Windows Server 2016 through 2025 and Windows 10 and 11 as applicable. WSUS supports Unified Update Platform updates for Windows 11 clients only after installing an update or adding MIME types in IIS. The product is deprecated and gets no new features, yet remains supported for production with security and quality updates according to its lifecycle.

zero-hour-auto-purge.title: Zero-hour auto purge (ZAP) in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 – Microsoft Learn
zero-hour-auto-purge.notes: Zero-hour auto purge in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 detects and neutralizes phishing, spam or malware messages after they have already been delivered to cloud mailboxes. It exists because signatures are updated continuously yet harmful mail can still arrive, for example zero-day malware or content that becomes malicious only after delivery. ZAP keeps watching for signature updates and acts on messages already in mailboxes, and users are not notified when it moves one. Malware goes to quarantine, high-confidence phishing always goes to quarantine, other phishing follows the anti-spam policy action, and spam is handled only if still unread, following the policy verdict. It covers cloud mailboxes only, not on-premises ones, and can also act on malicious Teams chat messages. No special license is needed for email ZAP, while ZAP for Teams requires Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2. Limits: only recently delivered messages, the last 48 hours, are examined; allow lists and transport rules can override actions; some exceptions apply to advanced delivery policy entries. Activity appears in the mailflow status report and Threat Explorer.
